sentences.text: 1 The petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a road traffic accident filed petition under Sec.166 of I.M.V. Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents No.1 and 2 who are owner and insurer of a car No.KA-51-MN-4292 asserting that on 03.05.2022 at 03.00 PM when riding the motorcycle No.KA-01-HS-4030 on Attibele-Anekal road, opposite to Kusuma Farm, near Mayasandra, driver of the car No. KA-51-MN-4292 negligently drove the same, dashed the same to motorcycle thereby caused accident caused injuries to the petitioner.
Petitioner took treatment at Ganga Speciality Hospital, Anekal by spending Rs.5,00,000/-.
As on the date of the accident petitioner being aged 26 years use to earn Rs.30,000/- per month by working as Office Assistant at DHL Co., Mayasandra.

Regarding the accident Attibele Police registered Crime No.153/2022 against the respondent No.1 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.
279, 337 of PC.
2.

In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of the accident,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, age, occupation of the petitioner.
3. Inspite of service notice, respondent No.1 owner/ driver of the car No. KA-51-MV-4792 remained absent.

4. On the basis of the pleadings on 06.02.2023 this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 03.05.2022 at about 03.00 p.m., opposite Kusuma Farm near Mayasandra on Attibele-Anekal Road in Attibele, Bengaluru, he being the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-01/HS- 4030 had met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51/MN-4292 by its driver and he sustained injuries in the accident as averred?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation and if so, what amount and from whom?
3. What order?
5. On 12.06.2023, 27.06.2023 petitioner deposed as PW.1 and produced 13 documents at Exhibits P.1 to P.13.

On 25.07.2023, 13.09.2023, 17.10.2923 petitioner produced evidence of Medical Record Technician of Ganga Speciality Hospital, Dr. N. Chaithanya Babu as PW.2 & 3 and get produced 5 documents at Ex.P14 to P18.
6.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

7. On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.4,04,748/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
Muniraju.M vs Krishnappa.N on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153148964/
2 REASONS 8. Issue No.1:- In the evidence affidavit, petitioner/ PW.1 stated that on 03.05.2022 at 03.00 PM when riding the motorcycle No.KA-01-HS-4030 on Attibele-Anekal road, opposite to Kusuma Farm,
near Mayasandra, driver of car No.KA-51-MN-4292 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the motorcycle No. KA-01-HS-4030 thereby caused accident and caused injuries to petitioner.
9.
In the written statements, respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding the reason and mode of accident.
10. In the cross-examination, petitioner/PW.1 stated that during the accident he alone riding the motor cycle from Anekal towards Attibele.
PW.1 denied denied the suggestion that in the accident front part of the motorcycle has been damaged.
PW.1 denied the suggestion that as per Motor Vehicle Accident Report marked at Ex.P3 rear bumper of the car has been damaged.
PW.1 denied the suggestion that as the accident taken place due to his negligence after 2 days filed the complaint.
PW.1 stated that police had recorded his statement in the hospital.

11. In the evidence PW.2 produced copy of the MLC Register Extract and copy of the Police Intimation at Ex.P15 & 16.
12.
In the evidence PW.2 and 3 stated nothing regarding the reason, mode and consequences of the accident.

13. Ex.P1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to Crime No.153/2022 registered on 05.05.2022 by Attibele Police against the driver of the car No. KA-51- MN-4292 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279 & 337 of IPC, regarding the accident taken place on 03.05.2022 at 15.00 hours between motorcycle No.KA-01-HS-4030 and car No.KA-51-MN-4292 resulting in the injuries to the petitioner on the basis of the typed complaint signed by Yellamma W/o Muniyappa.
14. Ex.P2 is the copy of the spot mahazar recorded on 05.05.2022.

Ex.P3 is the copy of the Motor Vehicle Accident Report dated 10.05.2022 in which damage noticed on the rear part of the car No.
KA-51-MN-4292, front part of the motorcycle No. KA-01-HS-4030 by the Motor Vehicle Inspector are noted.
15. Ex.P4 is the copy of the Wound Certificate.

Ex.P5 is the copy of charge sheet filed by Attibele Police in crime No.153/2022 against Shivakumar S/o Venkataswamy, driver of the car No.
KA-51-MN-4292 for having committed offence punishable under Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.

In Ex.P15 & 16 copy of the MLC register extract, the history of the injuries noted as RTA in between DHL Company and Shubha Apartment, Attibele to Anekal road at 4 PM while going on two wheeler hit by four wheeler.
16.
In the file, there are no evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by petitioner regarding the reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 03.05.2022 at Muniraju.M vs Krishnappa.N on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153148964/
3 03.00 PM when petitioner was riding motorcycle No.KA-01-HS-4030 on Attibele - Anekal road,
Opposite to Kusuma Farm, near Mayasandra, Shivakumar S/o Venkataswamy negligently drove the car No. KA-51- MN-4292 dashed the same to motorcycle No.KA-01-HS- 4030 thereby caused accident and caused injuries to the petitioner. Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

In the evidence affidavit, petitioner/ PW.1 stated that in the accident he has suffered cut wound on chin region - comminuted fracture of body of mandible on either side paramedian location - fracture of anterior and posterolateral walls of both the maxillary sinuses - fracture floor of both the orbits - comminuted fracture of left squamous temporal bone - extra dural hematoma beneath the fracture left temporal bone and thin subdural hematoma noted along left temporal lobe and other multiple injuries, took treatment at Ganga Speciality Hospital, Anekal by spending Rs.6,00,000/- for medicine, conveyance, nourishment, attendant and required to take further treatment at the cost of Rs.50,000/-.
Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.30,000/- per month by working as Office Assistant.
18. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegations regarding the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
19. In the cross-examination petitioner/P.W.1 stated that after accident public have shifted him to Ganga Speciality Hospital, Anekal.
PW.1 denied the suggestion that the bill marked at Ex.P9(1) is not a complete bill.
PW.1 stated that DHL company his employer used to pay salary by cash.
PW.1 denied the suggestion that the companies will pay salary more than Rs.10,000/- by crediting the same to bank account.

PW.1 denied the suggestion that for the purpose of case created medical bills.
20.
In the evidence affidavit, PW.2 produced case sheet at Ex.P17.

In the cross-examination PW.3 submitted ignorance about the mode of payment towards hospital bills and submitted ignorance about the contents of the case file marked at Ex.P17.
21.
In the evidence PW.3 Dr. N.Chaitanya Babu stated that on 10.08.2023 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that the petitioner suffered disability at 40% to whole body.
In the cross-examination PW.3 submitted that he neither treated the petitioner nor taken opinion of the treated doctor nor verified case sheet of the petitioner.
22. PW.3 stated that he has verified the Wound Certificate and Discharge Summary of the petitioner.

23. Wound Certificate, Discharge Summary, case file, prescriptions, medical bills, case sheet and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered (1) cut wound on chin region,
(2) comminuted fracture of body of mandible on either side paramedian location, (3) fracture,
anterior and posterolateral walls of both the maxillary sinuses, (4) fracture floor of both the orbits,
(5) comminuted fracture of left squamous temporal bone, (6) 41*6MM extra dural hematoma beneath the fracture left temporal bone and thin subdural hematoma noted along left temporal lobe,
took treatment at Ganga Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 03.05.2022 to 10.05.2022 by spending approximately Rs.1,97,248/-.

In the copy of the Adhaar card marked at Ex.P6 date of Muniraju.M vs Krishnappa.N on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153148964/
4 birth of petitioner is noted as 12.10.1995.
In the file there are no documents regarding the quantum of the income of the petitioner.

As PW.3 is neither treated the petitioner nor verified case file about treatment taken by the petitioner evidence of PW.3 is not sufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income.

Hence, I award Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering,
Rs.1,97,248/- towards treatment charges, Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards attendant, nourishment and conveyance, Rs.77,500/- (15,500 x 4) is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period, Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities and unhappiness.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled to receive Rs.4,04.748/- with current and future interest @
6% p.a. as compensation/damages from the respondent No.1 & 2.
24.
In the written statement, the respondent No.2 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to car No. KA-51-MN-4292 as on the date of accident.
In the file there are no evidence to show contravention of any terms of the policy by the respondent No.1.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondent No.1 and 2 being owner and insurer of the car No. KA-51- MN-4292 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondent No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.4,04,748/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Four Thousand Seven Hundred Forty Eight only) with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioner as compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the car No. KA-51-MN-4292 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within three months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by him, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 11 th day of September, 2024)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
